t: Qiskit: What Qiskit Is: Programming Quantum Computers
title: Qiskit: What Qiskit Is: Programming Quantum Computers
description: Qiskit is the SDK for quantum computing: you build circuits from gates (Hadamard, CNOT, rotations), transpile them for real hardware topology, simulate them with Aer, and run them on IBM's quantum processors. It covers the full stack from textbook algorithms (Deutsch-Jozsa, Grover, QPE) to variational algorithms (VQE, QAOA) for near-term devices. For defense and research, it is the on-ramp to post-classical computation — the tool you learn before the hardware matters.

title: Qiskit: Qubits, Gates, and Superposition
description: The fundamentals: a qubit is a two-level quantum system in superposition; gates rotate the state vector (X flips, H creates superposition, CNOT entangles); measurement collapses to classical bits with probabilities from the amplitudes. Qiskit's circuit model makes this concrete — build the Bell state in four lines and watch the simulator return 00 and 11 with equal probability. Everything else is composition.

t: Qiskit: The Transpiler: Fitting Circuits to Hardware
title: Qiskit: The Transpiler: Fitting Circuits to Hardware
description: Real quantum chips have fixed qubit connectivity and native gate sets, so the transpiler rewrites your circuit: mapping logical qubits to physical ones, inserting SWAPs for connectivity, decomposing gates to the native set, and optimizing depth. Transpilation levels trade compile time for circuit quality. A circuit that simulates beautifully can die on hardware if the transpiler cannot fit it — the resource manifest (depth after transpiling) is the reality check.
key_facts: Map to physical qubits, insert SWAPs

title: Qiskit: Aer: Simulation Before Hardware
description: Aer's simulators — statevector (exact, up to ~30 qubits), density matrix (noise modeling), stabilizer (Clifford circuits), and MPS — let you develop without queueing for hardware. Noise models built from real device calibration make the sim honest. The workflow is simulate exact, simulate noisy, then hardware: each stage catching what the previous cannot. Most quantum development happens in Aer; hardware is the final exam.

t: Qiskit: Your First Circuit: Bell State to Hardware
title: Qiskit: Your First Circuit: Bell State to Hardware
description: The hello-world: build the 2-qubit Bell circuit, simulate with Aer (00/11 at 50/50), transpile for a real backend, submit the job, and read the counts — which show 00/11 dominant with noise-induced 01/10 sprinkled in. That sprinkle is the whole story of NISQ computing: the ideal answer, blurred by reality. Learning to read hardware counts with noise-aware eyes is the skill.

t: Qiskit: Algorithms: Grover, QPE, VQE, QAOA
title: Qiskit: Algorithms: Grover, QPE, VQE, QAOA
description: Qiskit's algorithm library spans the eras: Grover's search (quadratic speedup, the textbook triumph), quantum phase estimation (the subroutine behind Shor's), and the NISQ workhorses — VQE for chemistry and QAOA for optimization, hybrid loops where the quantum chip evaluates and the classical optimizer iterates. For defense-adjacent work, QAOA's optimization framing and VQE's materials science are the near-term relevance; Shor's is the long-term cryptographic thunderhead.

t: Qiskit: Error Mitigation: Living with Noise
title: Qiskit: Error Mitigation: Living with Noise
description: NISQ devices are noisy, so Qiskit invests in error mitigation: zero-noise extrapolation (run at amplified noise, extrapolate to zero), probabilistic error cancellation, measurement-error mitigation, and dynamical decoupling in the transpiler. Mitigation does not create fault tolerance — it squeezes better answers from noisy hardware. The discipline is reporting mitigated and unmitigated results together: the gap is the honest measure of the hardware.
key_facts: Both numbers published with the ledger

t: Qiskit: Quantum Machine Learning: QML Basics
title: Qiskit: Quantum Machine Learning: QML Basics
description: Quantum machine learning explores variational circuits as models: data encoded into qubit rotations, a parameterized circuit as the learner, measurement as the output, classical optimization of the parameters. Qiskit's machine-learning module provides the scaffolding (quantum kernels, variational classifiers). The honest status: fascinating research, no proven advantage yet on real tasks — but the toolkit is how you will know when that changes.

title: Qiskit: Defensive Uses: Quantum Readiness
description: Qiskit's defensive value is readiness: understanding what quantum computers will do to cryptography (Shor's vs RSA/ECC), to optimization (QAOA), and to simulation (quantum chemistry) — before it happens. Teams prototype post-quantum migration analysis, benchmark candidate algorithms, and train the workforce. Quantum readiness is not having a quantum computer; it is having people who understand the transition.

t: Qiskit: Pulse: Controlling at the Physics Level
title: Qiskit: Pulse: Controlling at the Physics Level
description: Below gates is pulse: Qiskit Pulse schedules the actual microwave pulses that drive superconducting qubits. Pulse-level control enables custom gates, error characterization, and the research frontier of optimal control. Most users never touch it; the ones pushing hardware limits live in it. The abstraction ladder — pulse, gates, algorithms — is the full stack, and knowing which rung your problem lives on is the expertise.

t: Qiskit: Debugging: Why the Counts Are Wrong
title: Qiskit: Debugging: Why the Counts Are Wrong
description: Quantum debugging classics: the transpiler mapped badly (check the layout), the circuit is too deep for the coherence time (check depth vs T1/T2), readout error dominates (apply mitigation), or the algorithm itself is wrong (verify in exact sim first). The ladder is exact sim, noisy sim, hardware — and the bug's location is whichever stage first diverges. Never debug the algorithm on hardware.
key_facts: Exact sim, noisy sim, hardware ladder

t: Qiskit: Runtime: Hybrid Loops at Scale
title: Qiskit: Runtime: Hybrid Loops at Scale
description: Qiskit Runtime co-locates classical computation with the quantum processor for variational loops — the optimizer runs next to the QPU, not across the internet. Sessions keep the allocation; primitives (Sampler, Estimator) are the interface. For VQE/QAOA at scale, Runtime is the difference between feasible and farcical. The cost model is quantum-seconds; the discipline is minimizing them.

t: Qiskit: Testing: Verification of Quantum Programs
title: Qiskit: Testing: Verification of Quantum Programs
description: Testing quantum code: exact-simulation oracles for small circuits, property tests (unitarity, reversibility), statistical tests on hardware counts, and the discipline of testing the classical scaffolding thoroughly (most bugs are classical). Formal verification of circuits is the frontier. The honest practice is stating what was verified and how — 'tested in exact sim to 12 qubits' is a claim with boundaries.

title: Qiskit: Real-World Pattern: Optimization Pilot
description: A complete pattern: a logistics team pilots QAOA on a routing subproblem — formulate as QUBO, test in exact sim, scale in noisy sim, run small instances on hardware, compare against classical heuristics. The result is usually 'classical still wins, but we learned the scaling' — which is the honest near-term outcome, and the team is now ready when the hardware crosses over.
